That is the best arrangement which we can make at present. What will happen in the future, I am not in a position to say.
Will there be two trips a week between Campbellton and Gaspe as at present?
There will be only twenty-six round trips-half the subsidy and half the service.

Have the people down
there expressed any desire for a service of that kind?	.

I have not had time to
communicate with the people, and it is not quite open to do in a few days' time what might 'be best for the service. If you have plenty of time to call for tenders and get competition in that way, you might do better. Here was a service which was about to open and that was the only proposition I could get placed before me and I took it up rather than have the service lapse.
Why not have the Canada continue the contract of last year?

That might have been
possible if I had had a proposition to continue it, but I had not.
You had a contract.

A contract is not much
use against a man who has died and whose estate is not prepared to carry it on. My hon. friend would not like me to press a service in a case of that kind.
I understand the boat has been sold to another company.
Yes.
What is the name of the new manager of the company?
The contract will be with the Gaspe and Baie des Chaleurs Steamship Company, .Limited, manager Mr. Blouin.
Is he a resident of Quebec city? '
I do not know.

I put a question to the minister some time ago about the state of the steamer Canada, whether she had undergone any inspection or not, and the Minister of Marine and Fisheries gave me the following information:
The SS. Canada was inspected by the Government inspectors and granted a certificate on the 5th May, 1913 ; this certificate expired on the 1st December, 1913. No further report of official inspection has yet been made to the department, and no certificate for 1914 has been issued.
This answer was given on the 6th of April, three weeks ago.

I cannot say whether a certificate has been issued since then or not. I have not any information that I can give my hon. friend. With reference to the other vessel to be put on, I made inquiries and an inspection of the vessel made to satisfy myself that she was able to carry on the other half of the service. I am informed by the Postmaster General that the Canada is in dock being repaired, and that, when repairs have been made, she will get her certificate. The vessel must get her certificate in order to run on the route.

I have, in a return brought down to the House on the 2nd of March of the present year, a letter from the late president of the company, who gave as his reason for going into dry-dock last year on the 28th of November, at an earlier date than usual, the fact that he had asked Lloyds, of London, England, to certify the vessel, and they had instructed him to place it in dry-dock and he had complied with their instructions. I would like the minister to make sure that he is putting a safe boat on that coast.
I certainly will do that.

This boat was bought in 1892. It was formerly called the Pro

Patria. It was reported as of no further use to the company which owned it, and lay in the harbour of Halifax for sale for quite	a	time	until	it was	bought
and	put on the Gaspe route.
The service was .not as bad as the one given by the Restigouche, but almost as bad; since the Admiral was taken off the route the service has been going from bad to worse. The Canada was patched up; a couple of cabins were built on the deck, but the machinery is out of date and she did not give satisfaction at all last year. The service used to be sixty trips during the season; that was cut down to fifty-three and it is now to be cut down to twenty-six, a trip every week. In the months of May and June, large quantities of salmon are taken from Gaspe to Charlo, transferred to Dalhousie and there put into the icehouses to be transported by rail. The people found the service of the Canada, two trips a week, entirely inadequate, and they organized local services. A resident of Bonaventure put on a special boat; the hon. member for Restigouche (Mr. Reid) sent a sailing vessel over from Chafflo and Loggies, I think, had an independent service of their owa AH these agencies were employed to carry the salmon taken up in May and June. The Canada gave a poor service, but if the service is to be made poorer stiU the people will have to rely on the railway to carry their fish. That is one more argument in favour of the suggestion I made the other night: that the time is coming when the Government should take over that railway and make it a branch of the Intercolonial. We spent a million and a half in cash upon that road and $250,000 were paid in special subsidies for the building of twenty-six iron bridges. The road between Carlisle and Gaspe, which was built at a cost of $3,000,000, is giving practically no satisfaction at all. During the winter only one train a day is run and for weeks at a time the country is without any service at all. The old line between Carlisle and Matapedia has to be rebuilt, but the chief requirement is a bridge between Cross and Campbellton to bring the Gaspe peninsula in touch with the International railway, with the Intercolonial at Camp-belltom and with the Transcontinental railway at Edmunston. If our friends in Nova Scotia get better steamship service for the carrying of their fish to the American market, we would have an ideal

'Service if we could but link up Gaspe with Carnpbellton. We could then take advantage of the International railway as well as of the Intercolonial system; we would be connected with the Boston and Maine and our fish could reach Boston within twenty-four hours. In the Baie des Chaleurs there are great possibilities. If the railway service were improved I think the steamship service could be dispensed with altogether from the freight point of view, though I would be sorry to see it go, because Gaspe coast is one of the most picturesque parts of the province of Quebec; during the summer season that district is one of the most attractive portions of eastern Canada. I know that difficulties present themselves to the Government but I hope that the inferior steamship service and ineffective railway accommodation- to which the people of the G-aspe peninsula are subjected will he taken into consideration by the Government and some improvement made.
My hon. friend knows that the Bill providing for the purchase of that railway was thrown out last year by the Senate.

The Postmaster General
knows well that if he brings in a measure now to take over that road I will support it.

I have paid a great deal oi attention to the route mentioned by my hon. friend, but the question is rather a difficult one. When I came to look for results I found that with a payment of a subsidy of $20,000, the amount of freight carried was only 1,600 tons. The question arises as to how much money you can expend otn a route which in some respects seems to be on the diminishing side. I gave only the $5,000 and continued the granting of that amount because of my love for the scenic properties of that beautiful stretch of water, which I always liked to see visited by tourists and travellers. However, situated as we were, I could not see anything better to do than that which I have done.

The minister knows, of
course, that although traffic on the Canada has decreased, that does not mean that the Gaspd peninsula is not progressing. If the steamship traffic has gone down, it is because the railway now reaches Gaspe and because there are three independent lines of steamers running from Montreal to Quebec. In the old days the Admiral was 186
sufficient to do the whole business; now the Canada, the Gaspesian, the Lady of Gaspd, the Cascapedia and Gaspe railway are all employed in the carrying of trade.
Steam service between Halifax anti west coast Cape Breton, calling at way ports, $2,000.

How far
north on the west coast of Cape Breton do as this boat go?

She goes to Pleasant bay.
Steam service between Halifax and Sherbrooke, $2,000.
Is there a contract for that service, and if so, with whom?
Yes, with W. J. Murdoch. The service has been running for some time. I think without subsidy. Last year it came under subsidy.

It received a subsidy
from the local government of Nova Scotia.
Steam service between Kenora and Fort Frances, $8,000.
This is an inland service. Would the minister give some explanation?

That has a peculiar history. I wonder if I would be betraying any confidence if I explained i-t. A certain minister at a certain time had for a long time been very much importuned to grant a service over this route but he fought against the principle of subsidizing services in interior lakes in Ontario as a doughty soldier in the interests of economy and what he thought was proper steamship service. But at last he had to give so many steamship services to the ports in Nova Scotia and New Brunswick that, in a rather irate fit or mood, upon a certain occasion he declared he would give one subsidy on this internal lake and river in Ontario as a bit of an offset for the number that he had to grant in Nova Scotia. I felt that I would not be doing honour to his memory if I did not continue that subsidy.

I do not want to be understood as objecting to the service at all.
Steam service from the opening to the closing of navigation in 1914 between the mainland and the Magdalen islands, $15,000.

This is a service
that takes in part of Frince Edward Island. If I understood the minister aright he said there was no increase in the rate since he took charge of the department. My information is to the effect that there is an increase in the rate.

My impression is exactly the opposite. One of the troubles I have been up against is in regard to this service which is peculiar in many respects. It is not a service of very great volume of trade and the trade that is carried on is of a peculiar nature in which a sympathetic captain may very much help and an unsympathetic one very much hinder.
I think the service is a good one.

Then we will start from a common basis that this service is a good one. I have gone carefully over the accounts of the service for the last two years with Mr. McClure, and I satisfied myself that something more would have to be given, in order to retain that vessel in this service. We have had several vessel s on that service and had chronic complaints on the part of the people of the Magdalen islands and of other portions as well, against the service. This vessel is, if anything, superior for that service; hut she has given a good service and the people are very anxious that the service should *be retained. I have come to the decision to add a little more to the service in ordier to keep it for the present year with the same vessel and the same captain. One of the difficulties I met with was that the rates to the Magdalen islands were so reasonable, so far reduced in fact, that there had to he a larger subsidy or an increase in the rates.

I was familiar with the granting of this subsidy five years ago and with the rates that were then especially stated in the contract, and I am in a position to know that there has been no change in the rates since, because the gentleman who is Tunning the service is performing tlhe contract -as it was made five years ago without any change. I have spoken to the minister privately about the .matter, as the service starts from my own town. I understand the minister has granted an additional sum but only for the year.
Yes.
What is file minister's policy in regard to the future?

These subsidies all around our coasts have been yearly subsidies. There are some difficulties to the department in the administration in having them fall in each year and so as soon as we have worked out some better system of checking up the receipts and expenditures we hope

to make a change and to enter into contracts for a period of years, perhaps three years or five years.
Steam service between Mulgrave and Guys-borough, calling at intermediate ports, $5,500.

I have bad requests
that the port of Sand Point, a place with a wharf on the strait of Oanso should receive a call from this steamer. It would have been easy to do but I find there is a difficulty in this way. A new wharf was erected there for the purpose o-f providing for .a call of that boat. Money was voted in the session of 1911 and a contract was made for .building the wharf. After the new Government came into power, the Minister of Public Works did not cancel the contract but he decided to change the site. The first site gave sufficient depth for the Steamer to call at the outer end of the wharf and do the business, but the minister changed this site to a point half a mile away, in order to give $160 to a friend of Ithe .party and to please some of his political friends who resided there.
Of course that is an assertion.

That is the only reason.
the consequence is that the Wharf is now no good to anybody, because there is not sufficient depth of water in front of it for any boat to call at low tide. I would like the minister to have a consultation with the Minister of Public Works, and if he can induce him to add 100 feet to that .wharf so as to give a sufficient depth of water it will be a great accommodation to the people of that locality.
I will consider the matter and have it fixed one way or the other: either get a little more water, or shave something off the bottom of the vessel.
Will the boat call at Big Pond?
Did it last year?
I am told by a resident there that it did in the first part of the season, but not in the latter.
I cannot say whether that is included in the contract or not, but I will make a note of it.
There is a Government wharf there.
Has it water?

I presume so.

Steam service-Pictou, Mulgrave, Chetieamp, $7,500.
Who has the contract this year?

I forget the name of the company, but it is the one in which Roderick McDougall is interested. I suppose my hon. friend wants some information on that matter. I have had more trouble over that than over any other service.
If the minister had consulted me, I could have helped him out very easily.

One never knows what silent and unobtrusive friends are close at hand to help out in times of difficulty, and often loses the aid he might have had. The facts of the case-I have them pretty fresh in mind-are these: The vessel was the City of Ghent-Captain Beatty. I remember the captain, and I have some recollection of the City of Ghent. 'So far as I can learn, the Ghent was a popular vessel, though not the best in the service, but the captain was not quite so popular as the vessel, and there was a great deal of trouble and many heartburnings. I took the ground at last that if I could get a suitable vessel and a suitable captain to cater to what seemed to be the wish of the customers of the route, that it was my . duty to do so. After a long while I found a sea-faring man who undertook to get a suitable vessel and to organize the service, and I have given him the contract for the present year. The vessel is the steamship Kinbum, refitted so as to give what seems to be sufficient accommodation for the route. We will try it out and see what happens this year.
I hope the minister will see that she starts from Pictou.

Oh, yes, and goes back
to Pictou every time.

If I have one
particular objection to the whole contract, it is that one fact that she starts from Pictou.

I have no hesitation in
saying that if I were making the service anew, I would start the vessel from Mulgrave and run that route. I would divide the service into two, and if it weie necessary put on a service from Pictou to Mulgrave, serving the points in Antigonish county between those two towns and also >864
run a boat from New Glasgow. But it is not possible for me to do that this year.

Here is another
case where the minister might have been helped out if he had consulted the representative of the county the year before last. The minister will not forget that he changed the service two years ago. Under the late Government there were two services. There was a boat from Pictou to Cape Breton ports, and a boat from Mulgrave to Chetieamp. The minister-I suppose from the standpoint of economy- undertook to amalgamate both services and gave the contract to Captain Beatty. If Captain Beatty did not turn out according to the expectations of the minister, he has himself to blame.

He was more energetic
than I thought he was.

If the service does not please the people of Inverness county they may blame the minister, because, as I have pointed out, it is impossible for one boat to do that service; and the same thing will happen again this year. The slightest consideration on the part of the minister would show him that it is an absolute absurdity for the boat to make one trip from Pictou to Chetieamp, and two from Mulgrave to Chetieamp in one week. On all that coast there is a large quantity of fresh fish, particularly salmon, and if we cannot have a regular two-trips-a-week service from Chetieamp to Mulgrave, the service is practically useless. We could not have it last year and certainly we cannot have it this year; the man simply cannot do it; the distance is too far. Another thing I want to point out to the minister is this: in my opinion the boat he has on the service now will not be any improvement on the service last year, and I question whether it will be as good.

She is not as good
a boat.

That is my information, and I think the department ought to have had that information-I had it long ago. The boat that was on three years ago gave satisfactory service and I venture to say there were no complaints against it; but the minister took that contract away and gave it to Beatty. He found no satisfaction in him and drove off that boat, and I venture to say that this third boat will be the worst of the three. The minister ex-

pects this boat to perform a service that is physically impossible.
The member for Peterborough says there are no impossibilities.

Let me ask the minister if he will be good enough to watch the service of this boat this year? Rather than have the Inverness service sacrificed, as it will be, I would suggest that Pictou be cut out altogether. I am very anxious to be connected with Pictou and we would have been connected with Pictou in a satisfactory way if the minister had not tampered with the conditions he found when he took charge. But he did tamper and the result is evident; we have now no service at all. If we are going to have a repetition of what occurred last year let him cut out Pictou altogether this year.
My hon. friend the member for Pictou and the member for Inverness can have a private conversation about cutting out Pictou.

There is another thing with regard to the passenger service at that point. I understand the Kinburn has been equipped with passenger accommodation. If it turns out that in two months' time this boat is not equipped what will be the result?

If my hon. friend tells me that the boat is not equipped, I will take some means of finding out whether she is equipped or not. She has to be equipped reasonably well for the service. My hon. friend will find that summer weather will make him less pessimistic than he is now.
'"Sir. CHISHOLM: I am not pessimistic; it is the people who are suffering, and not I.

I started out with the heroic idea of economizing and squeezing into one some of the many double services I found on that coast. I have had my experience with that matter-I am quite willing to admit it.
Did the minister get a report from any official as to the suitability of this boat for the service that it professes to perform ?

The boat was on the service from Halifax out to the southwest coast last year, but it had not sufficient passenger accommodation. Outside of that it had sufficient accommodation. It is in part a night service and there must be sleeping accommodation. I summoned the

superviser, who was in Ottawa at the time, talked the whole matter over with him and we came to a conclusion as to what would be reasonably good passenger accommodation. They must fulfil that condition or they will not get the subsidy.
Does the inspector, Mr. Tupper, report on the question of the suitability of vessels ?

Yes, of every vessel.
Steam service between Pelee Island and the mainland, $5,000.

The subsidy given so far has been 85,000. They have had for a series of years Tather an old
12 p.m. and not a very serviceable vessel, although it has done the work that it was necessary to do. This year the people of Pelee Island have subscribed their money, built a new vessel into which they have put about 870,000, they are going to give a better service and I am going to raise the subsidy to J8,000 for the improved service.
Steam service between Pictou and Montague, calling at Murray Harbour and Georgetown, $6,000.

There is a feature in connection with the services between one or two places to which I wish to call the attention of the minister. I think that in the contracts there is a clause to the effect that steamers subsidized by the Government shall use the Government wharfs where such wharfs exist. I think that is a proper clause.
If they have water.

I do not know of any wharfs in Prince Edward Island that have not water. This steamer does not use the Government wharfs, and the Government wharfs, as a rule, are better than the private wharfs. They have better freight sheds and are capable of giving better accommodation to the public. The hon. minister can understand that perhaps some of the shareholders, or some of their friends, may have a private wharf that the steamer people would like to use. I get letters in reference to this matter, and sometimes people who are aggrieved do not wish to make complaints personally.
At what ports?
At Montague there is an excellent Government wharf; it has a new freight shed and it should be used. I understand there is a clause in the contract to that effect.

I do not know whether
there is any clause in the contract or not, but I think the rule is that, if there is a Government wharf which is suitable for the people, the vessel has to call there if she is required to do so.

I would ask the minister to give notice to the steamship owners in time so that they cannot raise the plea that they were not notified and that they thought they could do as usual. Last year the steamer that called at Souris on the way from Pictou to the Magdalen islands did not use the Government wharf and a greater hardship was inflicted upon the people who shipped by the steamers in consequence of that than would have been the result even at Montague. A good deal of freight carried by that boat from Souris comes over the railway from Charlottetown and when the Government wharf was not used that freight had to be carted over from the Government wharf where the cars come down, around quite a distance to the private wharf, or it had to be carted from the station which was some distance back in the village land the goods had to pay unnecessary cartage and the double wharfage. Possibly this extra charge may have given rise to the idea that the freight Tates were increased. After considerable trouble last year I got that matter adjusted.
There is no longer a grievance?

I do not know whether
it may arise this year or not.
Do not greet possibilities; you know that the thing is all right now.
I can quite see that the minister does not take the matter seriously.
I am here to listen to you.
I am glad to hear that.

My hon. friend should not deprecate himself enough to think that in adressing his remarks to me he would not address remarKs which would receive serious attention. Every member of this House, on any side of it, that wants to say anything in reference- to any service in which he is interested has a right to be seriously treated, and I always so treat him.

I am glad to hear that. If the minister's method of answering me did not convey that impression it is my misfortune. I suggest to the minister
that he should give notice to the steamship owners that that clause in the contract will be carried out.
If there is a clause in the agreement and they have signed the contract and I have signed it, it will be carried out; there is no necessity of giving notice.

Lest there be any
misunderstanding, I tell the minister that in the case of Montague, the Government wharf was not used last year.
I shall be glad to inquire into that.
I see in one of those votes that you are subsidizing a schooner; is that a sailing vessel?
No, it is a motor boat.
Is it a new departure for the Department to subsidize motor boats for work of this kind?

It is pretty hard to say what would be a new departure in the application of these subsidies. The Ghent, which ran from Pictou to Northern Cape Breton, found it impossible to get into a number of the smaller ports along the Antigonish coast, and this small vessel ran from Glasgow, and performed a very useful service to the people of that locality. I have the letters of the merchants and the priests along that coast congratulating me for putting on the service, and telling me how important it was that the contract should be continued.
Who is performing that service?
I think the man's name is Macdonald; it is a small subsidy of $500 a year.

This opens up a new field for the exploitation of persons who desire to get their names on the pay-roll for Government subsidies. I realize that there are many situations similar to those described by the minister, where ordinary steamers would be unable to call at certain places on account of the shallowness of the water, and it would be very desirable to subsidize gasoline boats for that purpose. I am glad to see the minister has undertaken to supply this much-needed service, and I may say to him that it is quite possible that in the near future very many similar applications will be made.
I do not propose to extend the principle.

I may tell the minister that I know the rates have been increased on the service about which we were speaking, but I cannot be sure of the year in which the increase took place. Is the minister sure that no increase has taken place?

I can only say that my recollection does not warrant me in saying that as to that particular service a request for an increase in any of the rates has been made. The instructions are absolute, and the clause in the contract is absolute that they must not charge any higher rates without the permission of the minister. I 3o not recollect receiving any complaint on that score.
I know that some years ago they charged $5 a head for cattle, and I think the charge is now 57.50.

I do not think I should take the ground that the rates should remain the same over a period of years, during which there have been many essential changes in cost. I take it that what the contract means is that the rates shall not be increased beyond what is reasonable. There might occasions arise when the Department would think it reasonable to allow an increase.
I understood the minister to say there was no increase at all.
No increase, unless authorized.
I am not objecting to a reasonable increase, and perhaps there might be good reason for it in some cases.
I do not recollect any application for an increase.

Some years ago these
boats called at Souris on their way to Newfoundland., but that service was cut out, and they now call only at Summerside and Charlottetown. The subsidy was only $8,000 when they called at Souris and they are now getting $16,500. I think they should make a call at each county, in consideration of the increased subsidy.
The vote is $16,500, but it is regulated according to the number of calls they make, and for a series of years they have made calls which entitled them to $12,500 per annum.
If they called at Souris would they be entitled to $16,500?

My impression is that they would be entitled to more subsidy if they called at Souris, but I am not positive. I think there was correspondence on the point that they had not reserved space, and that therefore, the freight that offered' was not carried, and I took that matter up with them.
That would be at Charlottetown. Of course, it would be a great convenience to the people living in the neighbourhood if we could get at least one of these boats to call at Souris.
I have the impression that they declined to call at Souris unless they were paid more subsidy.

Well, we are voting a
larger amount than they have been receiving. Is the contract for one year only?
Yes.
Is there a possibility or a probability of getting the steamer to call at Souris during the coming season?
I do not know, I will take the matter up.
If not, we will try to have it next year.
Would my hon. friend have prepared a list of the rates of the different services that might be laid on the table of the House at a later date?

It could be prepared.
There would be seventy-five or eighty of them.
Merely the rates so that there would be no divulging of private information. It would be convenient for comparison. While the accommodation is important, the rate is also important.
I will see whether or not there can be prepared for the annual report a table which will give the rates.
That report would not be received until next session of Parliament.

We will try to get something for my hon. friend at an early date.
Steam service during the year 1914, between Quebec and Blanc Sablon, calling at ports and places along the northern shore of the river St. Lawrence between such terminals, $20,000.

Before this item passes, without complaining of the past, I want

to congratulate the Government, and principally the Postmaster General, who is the minister of the Quebec district, on the success they have had in getting to do this service, instead of poor people, a strong company which will give two boats, one of them being prepared to carry one hundred first-class passengers at fair rates, under the supervision of the Government, and ready to take all means possible t-o advertise the resources of the north shore which has been neglected until now. The people living along the north shore will appreciate this service; and, in their name and my own, I want to thank the Government, and principally the Minister of Trade and Commerce and the Postmaster General, for their work in bringing about this service, which will materially promote the prosperity of that part of the country.
It would be satisfactory to hon. members who are not present if the last item should stand to give them an opportunity to discuss matters in which they might be interested.

Any questions can be
asked on the former item that was allowed to stand.
Progress reported.
